Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment: audit window & pricing questions — initial deal desk assessment

Thanks for the context, Sergio. Quick assessment from Deal Desk:

- Audit window: We can accept a constrained audit window, but must add explicit scope limits and pre-notification requirements. Suggest: 30-day on-site window limited to predefined artifacts (authentication logs, config snapshots, encryption key access logs) and one annual visit. We will require at least 30 days' advance notice and an agreed itinerary.
- Keys: Customer-managed keys (BYOK) is acceptable, but we need legal/engineering wording to ensure Redwood cannot be compelled to export keys. We'll pull the SOC2 excerpt to align controls.
- Pricing: 25% off is aggressive for a first-time enterprise on-prem deal. For a 36-month commit we can consider up to 20% as a Deal Desk recommended cap, conditioned on: 1) a minimum quarterly commit (to preserve economics), 2) SOW that limits scope of support (no managed upgrades included), and 3) signature by the customer's CIO and our CRO/CEO or delegated exec.

Action requested: Laura — would you be comfortable approving a one-time exec concession up to 20% with the conditions above? If yes, I will prepare a clean redline and a one-page exec approval memo for signoff (including fallback: 15% + additional service fees).

I am attaching the SOC2 excerpt that maps to the key controls we referenced (SOC2_redwood_excerpt.pdf) for quick legal review.

-Karthik
Head of Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment: audit window & pricing questions — approval threshold

Karthik — thank you for the clear recommendation. I approve the Deal Desk recommendation: up to 20% discount for a 36-month committed term if the following are in place:

1) Minimum quarterly commit (specified in SOW) — customer to provide forecasted monthly token usage and a quarterly minimum spend equal to 80% of forecast.
2) SOW explicitly limits support scope (no managed upgrades, remote troubleshooting only) and caps on-site remediation events (max 2/yr paid at T&M rates).
3) Audit clause: 30-day annual on-site audit restricted to pre-agreed artifacts; 30 days' notice; Redwood may redact sensitive internal operational notes; Redwood legal to prepare a tightly-scoped exhibit.
4) BYOK: customer-managed keys acceptable; legal to confirm language protecting Redwood from key-export obligations.

Sergio — proceed to issue a counter with the above, capped at 20%. Karthik, please create the exec memo and include the SOW redlines; I will sign the memo on behalf of Commercial. We should require the customer's CIO signature and a PO from procurement to start the pilot.

Laura Bennett
VP Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
